terms.grammar: verb, first conjugation, deponent: alone, or with the accusative of the game
evidence: Cic. Fam. 2.11.2: quī vēnārī solent (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Also, figuratively, to hunt after something (votes: Hor. Ep. 1.19.37). Vēnātum īre, to go hunting (Verg. A. 4.117).

evidence: Caes. B.G. 4.1: multum sunt in vēnātiōnibus (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Also a beast-hunt staged in the arena (Cic. Off. 2.55) and the game that is caught (Liv. 35.49.6).
Feminine vēnātrīx. A hunting dog is canis vēnāticus (Plaut.; Traupman 330).

phrases.latin: vēnor aliquandō, sed nōn sine pugillāribus, ut quamvīs nihil cēperim nōn nihil referam
phrases.english: I hunt sometimes, but not without my notebooks, so that even if I catch nothing I bring something back

phrases.latin: Illīcne umquam vēnāris? — Etiam. Vēnor cunīculōs, phāsiānās, cervōs.
phrases.english: Do you ever hunt there? — Yes. I hunt rabbits, pheasants and deer.

phrases.source: Traupman 48; Cic. Verr. 2.4.31 (Lewis & Short s.v. vēnāticus)
